claim: The application must write Entries, then HardState and Snapshot, to persistent storage in that order, or write them together if the storage supports atomic writes.
quote: Write Entries, HardState and Snapshot to persistent storage in order, i.e. Entries first, then HardState and Snapshot if they are not empty. If persistent storage supports atomic writes then all of them can be written together.

locator: README.md, Usage, step 2 (also doc.go, Usage, step 2)
claim: No Raft message may be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk and all entries written by any earlier Ready batch; entries from the same batch may still be in flight while its messages are sent.
quote: It is important that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk, and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while entries from the same batch are being persisted).

locator: FAQ, Deployment, "Why an odd number of cluster members?"
claim: Quorum for n etcd members is (n/2)+1, and because adding a node to an odd-sized cluster always increases the quorum, an odd-sized cluster is preferred.
quote: An etcd cluster needs a majority of nodes, a quorum, to agree on updates to the cluster state. For a cluster with n members, quorum is (n/2)+1. For any odd-sized cluster, adding one node will always increase the number of nodes necessary for quorum.

locator: FAQ, Deployment, "What is maximum cluster size?"
claim: etcd has no hard theoretical cluster-size limit, but a cluster probably should have no more than seven nodes.
quote: Theoretically, there is no hard limit. However, an etcd cluster probably should have no more than seven nodes.

locator: README.md, Implementation notes (repeated in doc.go, Implementation notes)
claim: Because removing a member from a two-member cluster can leave it unable to make progress, the etcd Raft library recommends using three or more nodes in every cluster.
quote: This approach introduces a problem when removing a member from a two-member cluster: If one of the members dies before the other one receives the commit of the confchange entry, then the member cannot be removed any more since the cluster cannot make progress. For this reason it is highly recommended to use three or more nodes in every cluster.
